claims.summary: Over F_p, let C be a degree-D pseudoideal containing x^2-x for every variable. If deg q<=d, P=(1-q^(p-1))R and deg h+deg P+(p-1)d<=D, then q^(p-1)Ph lies in C. So for a Pang family with t>=1 choices q_j of degree <=d, P=prod_j(1-q_j^(p-1)), Delta=(p-1)dt and errors P g_i (deg g_i<=d), every q_j^(p-1) kills every error when (p-1)d+Delta+d<=D; for S families and any choice per family, the product of these Fermat killers, of degree <=S(p-1)d, kills every error when S(p-1)d+Delta+d<=D, and in the cube's vanishing ideal survives exactly when some cube point has every chosen q nonzero. Its degree bound S(p-1)d is below Pang's multiplier degree K exactly when S<K/((p-1)d), and it is not shown to survive in Pang's proper closure.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer; the general form, the comparison against Pang's multiplier degree K and the withdrawn sublinearity conclusion are its corrections.
claims.rationale: Measures the Fermat product construction on Pang's errors against Pang's multiplier; useful only for few families, with survival open in Pang's closure.
claims.next_action: Prove the reviewer's disjoint-block lower bound for every surviving common killer in the vanishing-ideal model.
